title: Keerthy Suresh's Dorothy Crosses ₹10 Crore, Tamil Cinema's 10th Hit of 2026
excerpt: The Karthik Subbaraj period drama bounced back on its second weekend to cross the success threshold, turning steady word-of-mouth into a rare mid-budget box-office win.
body:
• Keerthy Suresh's period drama Dorothy crossed ₹10 crore net in India by day 10, with a ₹12.01 crore worldwide gross — recovering its reported ₹10 crore budget, according to trade estimates.
  • The Karthik Subbaraj film collected ₹9.15 crore in its first nine days, adding ₹1 crore on its second Saturday (October 3) after minimal weekday drops.
  • Dorothy is positioned as the 10th successful Kollywood venture of 2026, and it sits at #9 among Keerthy Suresh's post-COVID theatrical grosses.
  • For diaspora audiences: the Telugu version, distributed by Rana Daggubati's Spirit Media, released October 2, and North American screenings expanded in week two after a $180,000-plus opening week.

The Success Verdict Arrives

Keerthy Suresh's Dorothy has crossed the line. The Karthik Subbaraj period drama, which opened on September 25, pushed past ₹10 crore net in India by its tenth day, with trade trackers reporting a ₹12.01 crore worldwide gross — enough to recover the film's reported ₹10 crore budget and claim what box-office trackers call the success verdict. It is positioned as the 10th successful venture for Tamil cinema in 2026.

The day-wise run shows remarkable stability rather than a big opening burst: ₹90 lakh on day one, ₹1.25 crore and ₹1.4 crore across the first weekend, then a flat weekdays run of ₹85, ₹85, ₹83 and ₹78 lakh, before bouncing back to ₹1.08 crore on the second Friday and ₹1 crore on the second Saturday, October 3. The nine-day total stood at ₹9.15 crore, with the film maintaining what trade observers describe as exceptional holds for a mid-budget release.

Context and Background

Dorothy is a crime drama set in 1990s rural Tamil Nadu, directed by Karthik Subbaraj and co-starring Sananth and Rishikanth, with music by Ilayaraja. The film had its world premiere at the 2026 Toronto International Film Festival, where it received a standing ovation — a notable return for Tamil cinema at the festival. It runs 146 minutes and was produced by Jyoti Deshpande, Guneet Monga and Achin Jain for Dhammam Films, Jio Studios and Sikhya Entertainment.

For Keerthy Suresh, Dorothy sits at number nine among her post-COVID theatrical grosses, comfortably ahead of Revolver Rita (₹3.99 crore) though well behind her biggest hits like Sarkaru Vaari Paata (₹137.95 crore), Annaatthe (₹106.77 crore) and Dasara (₹81.93 crore). Festival backing and consistent word-of-mouth did the heavy lifting here, rather than star-driven openings.

Impact and Analysis

Dorothy's run is a case study in mid-budget economics. Kollywood's 2026 scorecard has been dominated by bigger bets; a ₹10 crore film recovering its budget on theatrical alone — without blockbuster numbers — is exactly the kind of outcome that keeps filmmakers willing to back festival-friendly, content-driven projects. The minimal weekday drops suggest the audience that found the film liked it enough to recommend it, and the second-weekend recovery confirms it.

A note of caution applies to the numbers themselves: the day-wise figures are trade estimates reported by outlets like Koimoi, not official producer figures, and box-office reporting in Indian cinema remains an inexact science. Still, the direction of travel — a flat, leggy run rather than a front-loaded collapse — is consistent across trackers.

Diaspora Angle

Diaspora audiences have played a visible role in the film's second week. Dorothy crossed $180,000 in North America in its opening week, and exhibitors increased screenings heading into week two on sustained audience interest. For Tamil cinema fans abroad, it is one of the few festival-premiered releases to hold screens rather than vanish after opening weekend.

What's Next

The Telugu version launched on October 2, with a trailer event in Hyderabad on September 30 and distribution through Rana Daggubati's Spirit Media — a push to extend the film's leg beyond Tamil Nadu. Streaming rights and an OTT date have not yet been announced, and the film's digital premiere will be the next number to watch.
